answer: West African okra soup is a savoury dish made with chopped or grated okra, which naturally thickens the cooking liquid. Nigerian variations may include peppers, palm oil, greens, meat, fish or crayfish, and are commonly eaten with a starchy accompaniment known as a swallow. Ingredients and methods differ across communities.

facts.fact: Chef Lola describes combining minced and sliced okra to vary texture.
A Guardian recipe published on 16 March 2015 describes an okra-and-tomato-sauce tradition.
Google Arts & Culture documents Yoruba obe ila and Efik/Ibibio otong as regional labels for okra preparations.
Google Arts & Culture describes swallows including eba, fufu and pounded yam as soup accompaniments.
The Guardian Nigeria documents examples including ila alasepo and an okra-and-banga preparation.
Immaculate Bites' okra soup article dated 25 May 2023 includes an optional egusi variation.
